title: Current Electricity - Basic Concepts and Formulas
topic: Electric Charge, Current, Potential Difference and Resistance
subject: Combined Physics

questions.question: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A). One ampere is one coulomb of charge flowing per second.

questions.question: What is the unit of electric charge?
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C).

questions.question: Which formula relates charge (Q), current (I) and time (t)?
questions.explanation: Charge = Current × Time, or Q = It. This means charge flowing is the rate of flow (current) multiplied by the duration.

questions.question: A current of 2 A flows for 5 s. How much charge passes?
questions.explanation: Q = It = 2 A × 5 s = 10 C.

questions.question: If 30 C of charge passes in 10 s, what is the current?
What is the unit of potential difference (voltage)?
questions.explanation: Potential difference is measured in volts (V). One volt is one joule of energy transferred per coulomb of charge.

questions.question: Which formula defines potential difference (V) in terms of work (W) and charge (Q)?
questions.explanation: Potential difference = Work done per unit charge, or V = W/Q.

questions.question: If 12 J of work is done to move 3 C of charge, what is the potential difference?
A 9 V battery does 18 J of work. How much charge flows?
What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.question: Which formula relates voltage (V), current (I) and resistance (R)?
questions.explanation: Ohm's Law: Voltage = Current × Resistance, or V = IR.

questions.question: A resistor has 6 V across it and 2 A flowing through it. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: R = V/I = 6 V / 2 A = 3 Ω.

questions.question: A 10 Ω resistor has 5 A flowing through it. What is the voltage across it?
A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. What is the current?
Which statement about conventional current is correct?
options: It flows from negative to positive terminal
It flows from positive to negative terminal
It is the flow of protons
It is the same as electron flow
questions.explanation: Conventional current is defined as flowing from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a power source. Electron flow is in the opposite direction.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its length is doubled (same material, same thickness)?
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length. Doubling the length doubles the resistance.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled (same material, same length)?
questions.explanation: Resistance is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area. Doubling the area halves the resistance.

questions.question: A charge of 60 C passes through a lamp in 2 minutes. What is the current?
questions.explanation: First convert time: 2 min = 120 s. Then I = Q/t = 60 C / 120 s = 0.5 A.

questions.question: A potential difference of 24 V causes 8 C of charge to flow. How much work is done?
A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor for 10 s. How much charge passes?
